definition: The neuromuscular system is the part of an organism made up of nerves and muscles and the connections between them, called neuromuscular junctions. In this source, it includes muscles, their nerve supply, and the junctions where nerve endings contact muscle tissue.

reasons: The packet does not support the broad/general claim that the neuromuscular system is “the part of an organism made up of nerves and muscles” as a definitional statement; it only describes a neuromuscular system in the specific insect Chironomus vitellinus.

The claim that the connections between nerves and muscles are “called neuromuscular junctions” is not explicitly stated in the packet as a general definitional relationship (the packet uses the term “neuromuscular junctions” and investigates them, but does not define them as the connections between nerves and muscles).

The rest of the definition (“includes muscles, their nerve supply, and the junctions where nerve endings contact muscle tissue”) is only partially supported: the packet discusses innervation of labeled muscles and investigates NMJs, but it does not explicitly describe nerve endings “contact” muscle tissue in those exact terms.
